result.title: CASE: Complementary Articulation-Aware Speech Encoder to Enhance Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation
result.summary: General-purpose self-supervised speech encoders provide strong acoustic representations, but their pretraining objectives are not explicitly aligned with the visible articulatory dynamics required by speech-driven 3D facial animation. We propose CASE (Complementary Articulation-aware Speech Encoder), a complementary speech encoder adapted by contrastively aligning short speech clips with continuous 3D lip-mesh VQ-VAE latents. After adaptation, the geometry branch is removed, and the audio-only CASE representation is fused with the baseline SSL speech representation through residual cross-attention, while retaining the motion-decoder architecture and objective. Across four VOCASET baselines, CASE reduces mean lip vertex error by 2.8-6.0%, and mean full-face vertex error decreases in every system. Under the same fusion protocol, CASE yields lower mean LVE than the unadapted AV-SE stream on all four generators, with model-dependent margins. Because adaptation uses Korean speech-geometry pairs and evaluation uses English VOCASET, the result is consistent with cross-language downstream transfer under a shared English-pretrained audio-visual prior.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CASE：用对比学习把短语音片段与连续的 3D 唇部网格 VQ-VAE latent 对齐以适配语音编码器，推理时移除几何分支，仅将音频表示与基线 SSL 语音表示经残差 cross-attention 融合，用于语音驱动 3D 人脸动画。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「借助另一模态的紧凑 VQ-VAE latent 对齐编码器、随后移除该分支并在推理期只用融合表示」的训练与融合机制，可能为 LVR 中用视觉 latent 塑造内部状态、以及多流表征融合提供可核查的线索。
